S9.01.needs: a Free account or a paid account with a few library files
S9.01.note: Only library files were found in this picker; no project, model or skill search was found in it.
steps: Open a chat and click the files control in the composer (the Files menu).
Click the search field labelled "Search library files".
Type part of a file name.
Compare: the list narrows to matching library files. Expected also lists projects, models and skills; the code found only a library-files picker here.
S9.01.where: Chat composer > Files menu > Search library files

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

S9.02.note: The exact text of the model-name trigger button was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Open a new chat.
Click the model name shown under the composer.
Look for the list titled "Models" and click a different model.
Compare: the model name shown in the composer changes to the one picked. If saving fails the toast says the previous model remains active.
S9.02.where: Chat composer > model name at the bottom of the composer > Models

labels.text: Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it.

S9.03.needs: a Deep Research run; a connected app or file for the connector and file options
S9.03.note: Only the Deep Research plan card was found as a source picker; no source picker in the normal composer was found.
steps: Start a Deep Research request and wait for the plan card.
Read the line under the plan: "Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it."
Use the add-source control on the plan card to add a source.
Compare: the chosen source appears under "Sources for this run" and can be removed.
S9.03.where: Deep Research plan card > "Sources for this run" (add a source before the run starts)

S9.04.needs: a connector with two linked accounts
S9.04.note: Searched apps/web/features/connectors once for an account picker; found only ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx, which lists accounts, and no control to choose one for a task or chat.

S9.05.needs: a team workspace on the account
S9.05.note: The exact name of the account menu trigger was not confirmed; the switch shows a confirm dialog with "Switch anyway" and "Stay in this workspace".
steps: Click the account menu.
Open the submenu "Workspace".
Look for "Personal" ("Only you") and any team workspaces listed below it.
Click another workspace and read the confirm text if it appears; then compare the list and the active workspace with Expected.
S9.05.where: Account menu > Workspace > Personal (team workspaces listed under it)

S9.06.needs: a paid or Free account with at least one project
S9.06.note: The visible text of the project control button was not confirmed.
steps: Open a chat and click the project control in the composer.
Click the search field "Search projects..." and type a project name.
Pick a project from the list.
Compare: the list narrows as you type and the chosen project is applied to the chat.
S9.06.where: Chat composer > project control > Search projects...

S9.07.needs: a code session with a connected repository and the managed compute switched on
S9.07.note: The code is partial and gated by E2B settings (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts). Searched apps/web/features/code/components once for a repository picker: found only test files, no visible control.

S9.08.needs: a code session with a connected repository and the managed compute switched on
S9.08.note: The code is partial and gated by E2B settings (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts). Searched apps/web/features/code/components once for a branch picker: found only test files, no visible control.

S9.09.needs: a microphone and a speaker or headphones; a browser that supports output device selection
S9.09.note: The code lists output devices only; microphone and camera pickers were not found in this file.
steps: Click the composer button "Start voice mode".
On the voice screen, click the control labelled "Audio output".
Look at the list titled "Audio output device" and the entry "System default".
Pick another output device if one is listed and check that the next reply plays through it.
S9.09.where: Start voice mode (composer) > voice screen > Audio output

S9.10.note: No once-versus-always choice was found for tool approvals or site automation in the code read.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Account section.
Find the row "API keys" and open it.
Start creating a key and look at the "Scopes" checkboxes.
Compare: the chosen scopes are listed on the created key. A once-versus-always choice was not found.
S9.10.where: Settings > Account > API keys > create a key > Scopes

S9.11.needs: a second account in the same workspace
S9.11.note: The button that opens the sharing controls was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Open a project that you own.
Open its sharing controls (the control that shows "People with access to" the project name).
Click "Add people", pick one or more members, choose the access level and click "Add".
Compare: the added members appear in the access list.
S9.11.where: Project > People with access > Add people

S9.12.note: No "Once" option was found in the frequency list in the lines read.
steps: Open the schedules page (the sidebar label was not confirmed) and start a new schedule.
Open the frequency list and pick "Daily", "Weekly" or "Monthly", or "Custom Cron" or "Recurrence Rule".
Set "Repeat Every" and read the line "Reads as:" below the rule.
Save and compare the next run time with the chosen cadence.
S9.12.where: Schedules page > new schedule form > Repeat Every

S9.13.needs: a few files uploaded or generated in the account
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the search field "Search the library by name" and type a file name.
Open the control "Filter the library" and pick a filter.
Compare: the list shows matching files and open one by clicking it.
S9.13.where: Sidebar > Library > Search the library by name

S9.14.note: Searched LibraryView.tsx and SkillFileViewer.tsx: the expand and collapse tree found is for skill files, and the library folder list is flat. No nested folder tree in the user's files was found.

S9.15.needs: a chat that produced a spreadsheet artifact
S9.15.note: Sort is cycled by clicking a column header; the exact header text depends on the artifact's data.
steps: Open a chat whose answer produced a spreadsheet artifact.
Open the artifact in the Artifacts panel.
Click a column header in the table to sort; click again to change the sort.
Compare: the rows reorder by that column and the table scrolls.
S9.15.where: Chat > spreadsheet artifact > Artifacts panel > Worksheets table; click a column header to sort

S9.16.needs: a few files in the library
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the control labelled "Library layout" and pick the grid view.
Look at the files shown as cards.
Click a card to open it and compare with Expected.

S9.17.needs: images and videos in the library
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the filter tab "Images" or "Videos".
Click a picture or video tile; the viewer labelled "<file name> viewer" opens.
Use "Zoom in" / "Zoom out" for images and "Close file viewer" to leave; compare with Expected.
S9.17.where: Sidebar > Library > Images or Videos tab > open a tile

S9.19.needs: an account that can start an agent run
S9.19.note: The exact place the timeline sits in the chat was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Send a request that starts an agent run.
Watch the activity block under the reply while it runs.
Look at each step with its label and the elapsed time shown after it, like "Thinking · 12s".
Compare: the steps are in time order and each shows its state when the run finishes.
S9.19.where: Chat > an agent run's activity under the reply (step list with "Working" or "Thinking")

S9.20.needs: a signed-in account with some recent activity
S9.20.note: The panel is shown by AccountSection.tsx under a condition not read in full; newest-first order was not checked in code.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Account section.
Scroll to the panel titled "Recent activity".
Check the entries: sign-ins, changes and runs.
Compare the order: newest first is expected.

S9.21.needs: a few tasks in different states
S9.21.note: The board column titles were not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Open the Tasks page (the sidebar label was not confirmed).
Click the layout control "Task layout" and pick "Board".
Look for the columns per status.
Compare: tasks sit in the column for their stage.

S9.22.note: The gallery step counter text is built from a template in the file; "Step 1 of" is the start of it.
steps: Open the gallery (the route is apps/web/app/gallery; the sidebar label was not confirmed).
Click "Choose artifact type" and pick an artifact type.
Read "Step 1 of" and the dots, then click "Next".
Click "Create" on the last step and compare the count and the dots.
S9.22.where: Gallery > Choose artifact type > pick a type > Next

S9.23.needs: a new account (or a reset onboarding state)
S9.23.note: The wizard in the code has two steps (name and a description); a model choice or sign-in step was not found in it.
steps: Sign in with a new account, or open the welcome page.
Type a name in "Preferred name" and read "Step 1 of 2".
Click "Continue" to go to step 2 and click "Back" or "Finish".
Check the saved name in Settings.
S9.23.where: Welcome screen (/welcome) > Preferred name > Continue > Finish

S9.24.needs: a desktop-width window and an artifact
S9.24.note: The handle is shown only in the desktop layout.
steps: Open a chat with an artifact so the Artifacts panel opens.
Tab to the separator labelled "Resize artifacts panel".
Press the Left or Right arrow key and watch the split move.
Drag the same separator with the mouse and compare both panes.
S9.24.where: Chat > open an artifact > drag the "Resize artifacts panel" handle, or focus it and press Left or Right arrow

steps: Open an artifact that has more than one version.
Click the version counter in the artifact toolbar to open "Version history".
Click a version and then "Restore" on the one you want.
Compare: the artifact returns to that version and the list shows it.
S9.26.where: Chat > artifact toolbar > version counter (v<n>/<total>) > Restore

S9.27.needs: a code session that has file changes
S9.27.note: The name of the Changes panel tab was not confirmed; the panel is in apps/web/features/code/components/CodeChangesPanel.tsx.
steps: Open Code and select a session that has file changes.
Open the Changes panel for the session.
Click a file to read its diff with added and removed lines.
Compare with Expected; use the include or discard controls only as a test, and cancel if prompted.
S9.27.where: Code > a session > Changes panel > file diff with "Include in the commit:" and "Discard the changes to"

S9.28.needs: a Free account or paid account; a question that triggers web research
S9.28.note: Source rows open in a new tab (target=_blank), not inside the app. Clicking an inline citation chip is a separate control in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx and was not walked.
steps: Send a question that uses web research, so the answer has sources.
Under the answer, click the "Sources" button (or "Sources · N" when there are more than 3).
In the side panel on the "Sources" tab, read each source's title, site name, date and snippet.
Click a source row; it opens in a new browser tab.
Compare with Expected: title, origin and excerpt visible, and the source opens.
S9.28.where: Chat answer > "Sources" button under the answer (aria-label "View N sources") > panel tab "Sources"

S9.29.needs: a Free account or paid account
S9.29.note: The account menu entry is the "Settings" item in apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx; the exact name of the button that opens the account menu was not confirmed. The bar detail text is built in code ("% used" is a template string), so the exact visible wording is not a literal.
steps: Open the account menu and choose Settings.
Click "Usage" in the Settings list.
Read the usage bars: each shows its label, "% used" and a reset time in the detail line.
Check that the bars are readable by a screen reader (each bar has an aria-label such as "<label> usage" and an aria-valuetext).
Compare with Expected: per-window meter with reset time.

S9.30.needs: a Free account or paid account
S9.30.note: The code line BillingSection.tsx:988 points to saved payment cards, not the credit balance; the credit balance card is in UsageSection.tsx.
steps: Open Settings and click "Usage".
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read the "Purchased credits" and "Bonus credits" rows.
Click the "Buy credits" button beside the card title; it opens Settings > Billing.
Compare with Expected: purchased balance shown with a way to add credits.

S9.31.needs: a Free account or paid account; a connector that uses OAuth scopes (otherwise a short "This provider does not use OAuth scopes" message shows)
S9.31.note: The "Before you connect" notice and the scope list show in different states (not connected versus connected); the code does not confirm which connector state shows which panel on one screen. Autonomy and allowed sites were not confirmed as shown in this view.
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Click a connector that shows a permission list.
Read the "Permissions requested" list: each scope has a sentence and a "Read" or "Write" badge.
Read the "Before you connect" notice and the "Tool permissions" button for the allowed tools.
Compare with Expected: plain-language view of what the connector may do.
S9.31.where: Settings > Connectors > select a connector > "Permissions requested" panel

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S9.32.needs: a paid account or a connected app that triggers approval; a prompt that makes the assistant use a tool
S9.32.note: The approve and deny button wording was not read; the allow label comes from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-presentation.ts. Whether a tester can trigger this depends on the account's tool setup.
steps: Use a chat where the assistant asks to run a tool that needs approval (for example a connected app action).
Read the inline card: it names the tool and shows "This tool requires approval before execution."
Use the card's allow button (label from TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS, not read as visible text) or the deny control if shown.
Watch whether the run continues or stops after the choice.
Compare with Expected: an inline card with approve and deny that resumes or stops the run.
S9.32.where: Chat > a message where the assistant wants to run a tool > approval card text "This tool requires approval before execution."

S9.33.needs: a paid account or a Free account; an outside account for a real connection (Google, GitHub or similar); an expired connection to see "Reconnect"
S9.33.note: No visible word "Expired" was found for connector cards; the expired state is shown as a "Connection issue" warning with a Reconnect button (SettingsModal.tsx).
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Use the tabs "All", "Connected" and "Not connected" to filter the list.
Open a connector; the header button shows "Connected" when linked, or "Reconnect" when the grant needs reconnecting.
For a connected connector, check the "Disconnect" action; for a not-connected one, check the connect action.
Compare with Expected: state shown on each card, and the connect or disconnect action.
S9.33.where: Settings > Connectors > each connector card (status shown as "Connected", "Not connected" or "Reconnect")

labels.text: Turn off tools to use this free model.

S9.34.needs: a Free account (free models) or a paid account with a model that has limits; an image or file to upload
S9.34.note: The notice shows only when the model catalogue is closed (ComposerFooter.tsx). The model picker's own visible label was not read.
steps: In the chat composer, open the model picker and choose a free model.
Attach an image or a file, or keep tools turned on.
Read the notice above the message box (role status, labelled "Model compatibility"): it says, for example, "Turn off tools to use this free model."
Remove the attachment or turn tools off, and check that the notice goes away.
Compare with Expected: a visible warning before sending when the model cannot handle the request.
S9.34.where: Chat composer > model picker (below the message box) > choose a model that lacks a feature > notice "Model compatibility" above the message box

S9.35.needs: a paid account or a Free account that can start a task; a task that runs several steps
S9.35.note: The toolbar button that opens the work-session panel was not located by its visible label; only the toggle code in WebChatPage.tsx was found. The Pluralised work-session dock label comes from TASK_DOCK_PANEL_LABEL in the same file.
steps: Start a task in chat that runs steps (for example a coding or agent task).
Open the side panel for work from the chat toolbar; the panel is labelled "Chat details" (or the work-session dock label on agent-work conversations).
Watch the card: it shows the current state, steps done and latest action, and updates while the run is going.
Compare with Expected: state and progress that update while the task runs.
S9.35.where: Chat > side panel "Chat details" (work-session panel) during a running task

S9.36.needs: a question that makes the assistant send an interactive card (choices or app card)
S9.36.note: InteractiveCardBlock.tsx renders the widget, and WebChatPage.tsx wires the resume handler, but no visible control label was found. The MessageBubble.tsx:2020 reference is not in the file now. The trigger for an interactive card in a normal chat is not confirmed from code.

S9.37.needs: a signed-in account that has notifications (unread ones give a count on the bell)
S9.37.note: Newest-first ordering comes from the feed hook, not checked in detail. The bell sits in SidebarBrandRow.tsx.
steps: Sign in and look at the sidebar top row, next to the wordmark.
Click the bell; the panel titled "Notifications" opens, newest first.
Look for unread items: they show in a bolder weight, with a count badge on the bell and ", unread" for screen readers.
Click an item that has a link; it opens its page and is marked read. Or click "Mark all as read".
Compare with Expected: list newest first, unread marked, open or mark read.
S9.37.where: Sidebar > bell icon beside the AGI wordmark (labelled "Notifications") > list > "Mark all as read"

S9.38.note: The Cmd+K binding is in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx (capture phase); the palette itself is mounted in apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx.
steps: On any page after signing in, press Command+K (Mac).
Read the search box with the placeholder "Search chats and actions".
Type part of a command, for example "settings", and watch the list narrow.
Use the arrow keys to pick "Go to Settings" and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: list filters as you type and Enter runs the choice.
S9.38.where: Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows or Linux) on any page > command palette
